Meta was formed in 1984 as a spin out from an engineering research project at the world famous Oxford University. The original project was aimed at developing laser sensor guided robot welding. This work was described in the original

One early success was a large project to develop sensor guided adaptive multipass robotic FCAW for a number of welding systems for Caterpillar, USA. These systems were in production for nearly twenty years. These systems were described in a widely referenced article (
Another early success was a welding cell for rocket nozzles for the European Ariane space programme. Much later Meta provided further systems for the Ariane programme, which can be seen as a video at
, as well as a number of systems for the Chinese space rocket engine programme.

Later, Meta also became heavily involved in pipe mill welding, providing hundreds of laser sensor system and even complete mill control systems. Meta is widely acknowledged to be the world leader in providing laser sensors for pipe welding and similar applications.

Overall, Meta has now provided over 3,000 laser sensors and continues to develop new and improved solutions for all common arc welding applications. From its early days with just a few people, Meta has grown to over 40 people from a wide variety of countries and backgrounds.
Thanks to its unique DLS sensor family Meta is acknowledged to be the leader in multipass SAW for energy applications, including pressure vessels, rotors, wind towers and monopiles.

Many welding applications in the transport industry are for very long welds, as shown here in this railway carriage application. Another similar example is the shipyard panel line. There is usually some distortion in the way the parts are prepared or fitted together which means that a weld tracking system is required. Meta has experience in many different transport welding systems.

The aim of the original research project at Oxford University, which was spun out to form Meta, was to develop a laser vision system for robot welding in the auto industry. Since we are still very active in that same industry thirty years later with many hundreds of systems installed, it seems that the project was successful.

QiOVA develops and markets laser marking and micro-machining products for the industrial sector. The company offers products such as the VULQ1-S FLASH and VULQ1-S BEAMS, which utilize multibeam technology for laser marking. QiOVA's products are used in various industries, including medical, luxury goods, and packaging. It was founded in 2011 and is based in Andrézieux-Bouthéon, France.

SharpLase provides laser marking and engraving technologies within the manufacturing sector. The company offers laser machines, including fiber and solid state lasers, for engraving, cutting, and marking various materials. SharpLase's products are used in industries such as medical, aerospace, automotive, and consumer electronics. It was founded in 2009 and is based in Monterey Park, California.

WeldTrace is a company that provides welding management software for the fabrication industry. Their offerings include tools for managing welding procedures, welder qualifications, and tracking, mapping, and inspection processes. WeldTrace serves the fabrication and engineering sectors and integrates with quality management systems. It was founded in 2007 and is based in Queensland, Australia.

KMLabs operates in ultrafast laser and x-ray science within the laser technology industry. The company provides ultrafast laser sources, including extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) lasers, along with femtosecond and attosecond laser systems. KMLabs' products are used in scientific and research applications. It was founded in 1994 and is based in Boulder, Colorado.
